paragraphs.text: Viashino is an obsolete red creature type . It was predominantly used for cards depicting intelligent bipedal humanoid lizard -folk. The type was made obsolete , and all past cards were given errata to be lizards with the release of Modern Horizons 3 to be more consistent with how other humanoid animals are typed.

Viashino are descended from Dragons , over whom they exert some power. Viashino possess lean but muscular builds and can be agile, quick, and vicious when necessary. They don't stop growing throughout their lives. They generally come in shades of green, brown, and red, and prefer arid climates. Viashino have gray blood. With few exceptions, they have three-toed feet and four-fingered hands. They are digitigrade and do not prefer stairs, instead using notched poles or ropes. They do not sit like humans, and it is said that they rarely lie down — even when sleeping — preferring instead to rest against a wall and prop themselves up with their tails.

Before they appeared on cards, the viashino were featured in the novel The Prodigal Sorcerer , a year before Mirage was released. The Viashino were a creation of Mark Sumner for this novel, and the team behind Mirage liked them enough to incorporate them into the game. A likely prototype of the creatures, the Viashin, appeared in Sumner's short story "Storm Winter", published in Dragon Magazine #163. Viashino were introduced to the game in Mirage .

The Lizard Warrior from Portal depicted a Viashino but lacked the subtype . The creature type returned in Visions , Urza's Saga and later sets. Mark Rosewater 's opinion is that it was a mistake to create the Viashino subtype for the Lizardfolk.

With the release of Laughing Jasper Flint in Outlaws of Thunder Junction , it was revealed that the Viashino creature type had been changed to Lizard. Rosewater noted that the creatures were still Viashino from a flavor standpoint. He expected previous Viashino to receive the Lizard errata as well. This was implemented with the release of Modern Horizons 3 .

On the Alaran shard of Jund , the viashino possess a crocodilian form. Viashino are fairly unintelligent and have minimal society. They form self-organized hunting bands referred to as thrashes that live and hunt in well-defined territories in the swampy lowland jungles. Brute strength determines who leads the thrash, and once established, the leader makes all decisions for the viashino in his band. The personality of the leader affects how the thrash hunts and where it lives. When a leader is killed, a thrash often will change its name and move to a new hunting ground. Viashino males generally lead the thrashes: they are heavy-set, muscular creatures that resemble humanoid alligators. The whole group is nomadic, though, so the females also hunt and fight — and when they’re protecting clutches of eggs, they can overpower males larger than themselves. Known thrashes include:

Manytooth Thrash: This thrash prides itself on the might and viciousness of its warriors. They seek out other thrashes against which to test themselves, and over time have earned a very large territory for themselves. The Manytooth have a coming-of-age ritual that involves young viashino fighting to the death for the right to become full-fledged warriors of the thrash.

Palehide Thrash: This thrash prides itself on slaying humans, which they call "palehides." They're aggressive and largely nomadic, following what weaker human tribes they can find. Their leader is an old, brittle-scaled viashino named Igh who claims to have personally slain three hundred humans in his lifetime.

Pitch Thrash: This thrash rules a vast network of low-lying tar pits known as the Seethe. Leadership changes often; the black mana of the Seethe causes these viashino to be more treacherous and merciless than other thrashes. The thrash specializes in running its prey into the pits and trapping them in the quagmire.
Thunder Thrash / Skyclaw Thrash

Viashino are masters of the ambush, lying in wait for beasts or human hunting parties. Sometimes a viashino party will raid a human settlement, stealing children or other objects of value to lure the humans onto the canyon floor. The viashino conceal themselves in the murky channels that wind across the jungle floor, sometimes for days, waiting for the warriors to pass.

On the shard of Grixis , necromancers have found the remains of viashino and resurrected them as zombies or skeletons . After the Conflux , the Viashino of Jund were confronted by their primitive, beastly, counterparts on Naya .
Viashino weapons are simple, usually clubs studded with chips of obsidian or teeth.
Kikkach: The paddle-shaped club lined with the teeth of crocodiles or predatory dinosaurs is called a kikkach, which means "rasping tongue" — like that of a great cat.
Sshak: A sshak is a crude axe carved from a large animal's bone, with chips of obsidian along the cutting edge. The name is an onomatopoeic name for the sound of its strike.
Challik: Some viashino use a type of grappling hook that launches jagged, heavy stones attached to cords that let them draw in entangled prey. The word challik translates as "toad's tongue."

On Capenna , viashino are more draconic than lizard-like, to the point of some possessing breath weapons. They appear to have a strong reverence for their draconic origins, with many joining the Riveteers in hopes of "unleash[ing] their own inner dragons" under Ziatora 's leadership. They mainly live in the Caldaia .

In Dominaria , viashino are said to have been created by Terrent Amese . However, viashino were shown to be present on the plane already during the Time of the Thran , which either indicates that the Terrent Amese creation story is pure myth, or that this event happened much earlier than otherwise thought. The main viashino civilization is on the Shivan sands. In addition to Shiv, they may be found throughout the Burning Isles and as far west as Jamuraa . With no hereditary ranks or titles, the viashino live in clan communities, each of which is led by a bey voted on by its citizens. They have a society of warriors. They live almost exclusively in simple desert camps, which can disappear in minutes if they decide to mobilize. Despite the emphasis on militarism and their warrior code, the viashino are also known for their metalsmithing and crafts. As harsh as the desert is, the viashino are suited to it, relying on "sand swimming" for transportation and tactical advantage.

Viashino have constantly been skirmishing with the Goblins , which are also native to Shiv, the Ghitu tribe of humans , and even the Shivan dragons themselves. In the face of any outside adversity, the viashino often became staunch allies of the goblins and the Ghitu . The four species have now formed the Shivan Nation together.
A cold-blooded species, the viashino survived the Ice Age by hiding within the Mana Rig .

The Viashino of Tamingazin mostly live in the city of Berimish. They don't know their gender until they reach maturity, but most have a preferred gender pronoun regardless. Females are marked by a network of yellow-green lines along their head and neck. Older viashino retire to the "breeding house". Like most viashino, they have four-fingered hands, but they uniquely have two fingers in the center and a thumb on each side. Despite their eight digits, they count in tens like humans.

The En'Jaga of Tamingazin are possibly related to the viashino. They are twice as tall as a human, with gray-scaled skin and fangs as long as a human hand. Their eyes are flat black, and they have forked tongues. They are native to the Great Marsh and the mountains west of Berimish , and are known to visit the city to trade.
Gastal ’s viashino are large and muscular, with spikes protruding from their skin.
The viashino of Karsus populate the plane's Mirrored Depths.

Ravnican viashino can be found throughout society, whether among the general guildless population (such as Tin Street Gossip or The Muckslinger Gang ), or as members of one of Ravnica's Guilds. Guild-affiliated viashino are most often found within the Boros Legion , Gruul Clans , and Izzet League .
A large planeswalker with lime-green skin.
